Print, summarize, compare, and extract from a fitted model

Source: R/radish_optimize.R
terradish_methods.Rd

S3 methods for working with fitted objects returned by terradish and summaries returned by summary().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
summary(object, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.terradish'
print(
  x,
  digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L),
  signif.stars = getOption("show.signif.stars"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
fitted(object, type = c("response", "distance", "covariance"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
simulate(
  object,
  nsim = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  method = c("permutation", "parametric"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
anova(object, ..., alternative = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
AIC(object, ..., k = 2)

# S3 method for class 'terradish'
residuals(object, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted terradish object.

digits

Number of digits to print.

...

Additional arguments passed through to generic methods.

object, alternative

Fitted terradish objects.

conf.level

Confidence level for nuisance-parameter confidence intervals reported by summary(). These intervals are conditional on the fitted conductance surface. confint() calls the same quantity level; conductance() and plot() call it quantile.

signif.stars

Should significance stars be printed in coefficient tables?

type

Type of fitted values to return: "response" (default) gives the expected response matrix on the scale of the data (genetic distance or covariance, according to the measurement model), "distance" gives the fitted resistance distances among focal sites, and "covariance" gives the fitted graph covariance (the focal-site block of the generalized inverse of the graph Laplacian).

nsim

Number of simulated response matrices to generate.

seed

Optional random seed used by simulate().

method

Simulation method. Only "permutation" (default) is implemented: it adds the residual matrix, with sites permuted jointly in rows and columns, to the fitted response. "parametric" is reserved and currently stops with an error.

k

Penalty multiplier supplied to AIC().

Value

  • print() returns its input invisibly after printing it.

  • summary() returns a list of class summary.terradish (also summary.radish). Its main elements are ztable (conductance estimates on the log-conductance scale, standard errors, z values, and p values), vcov and vcor (their covariance and correlation matrices), phi and phi_table (nuisance-parameter estimates, standard errors, and intervals on the measurement model's scale, conditional on the fitted conductance surface), phi_vcov, phi_at_bound (flags for kernel weights at zero), convergence, boundary and no_structure_boundary, loglik, df, aic, gradnorm, fcalls, iters, diagnostics, call, and dim. ibe_ratio holds the output of terradish_ibe_ratio (zero rows without environmental terms). Gaussian scale fits add sigma_table, with one row per smoothing scale: the estimate and standard error in map units, the fitting bounds, and a near_bound flag for estimates within one percent of a bound. Spline fits add spline_monotonicity.

  • coef() returns a named numeric vector of fitted conductance coefficients on the log-conductance scale, or an empty vector when they are unidentified.

  • fitted() returns a numeric focal-site matrix of expected responses, resistance distances, or graph covariances, selected by type.

  • simulate() returns a numeric response matrix for nsim = 1, or a three-dimensional array with simulations along the third dimension otherwise.

  • anova() returns a matrix of class anova, comparing two nested fits by log-likelihood, parameter count, likelihood-ratio statistic, and its reference-distribution p-value.

  • logLik() returns a numeric scalar of class logLik, with parameter-count (df) and focal-site-count (nobs) attributes.

  • AIC() returns \(-2\ell + kK\), where \(K\) is the number of estimated parameters; the default k = 2 gives Akaike's Information Criterion. Smaller values favor a fit when response and likelihood are comparable.

  • residuals() returns a numeric matrix of observed minus fitted responses, centered on both site dimensions for covariance-response models.

Details

Reading summary(). The coefficient table reports each conductance coefficient on the log-conductance scale with its Wald standard error, z value, and p value; exp() of an estimate is the multiplicative change in conductance per unit of the covariate. Use confint() for intervals on the conductance coefficients. The nuisance table reports the measurement-model parameters with conditional Wald intervals.

Parameter names repeat across measurement models with different meanings. In mlpe and leastsquares, tau is the log residual precision. In wishart_covariance and generalized_wishart, tau is the nonnegative multiplier on the graph covariance and sigma is the log nugget variance. See the parameter glossary in terradish-package.

Nuisance-parameter estimates and intervals from summary() remain on the parameterization used by the measurement model. For example, MLPE tau is log precision and its stored rho is unconstrained; the actual shared-site correlation is \(\text{plogis}(\rho)/2\). Consult the selected measurement-model help page before interpreting phi. For a verified numerical zero residual-variance limit in a Wishart fit, summary() retains the finite log-scale representation of sigma but suppresses its Wald standard error and interval. A zero residual variance does not imply a zero graph contribution. Covariance-response residuals are centered on both site dimensions: \(H(S-\Sigma)H\), where \(H\) is the site-centering matrix. Fitted covariance matrices retain their full \(n\times n\) form.

anova() is a likelihood-ratio test for nested conductance formulas fitted to the same response, sites, graph domain, conductance-model factory, and measurement model; Wishart fits must also use the same nu. Both fits must record successful outer and final nuisance convergence; missing diagnostics require refitting. The function checks formula-term nesting, but the analyst must still verify that the full measurement and conductance parameterization is substantively nested. Its chi-squared reference distribution assumes the tested parameters are regular interior parameters. It can be unreliable when a null value is on a parameter boundary or other regularity conditions fail; use a justified alternative or simulation calibration in those cases. One boundary case is handled automatically: when the larger model adds only Wishart environmental kernel weights (lambda_*, which are bounded at zero), anova() warns and reports a chi-bar-square reference with binomial weights instead of the ordinary chi-square. The table heading names the reference distribution that was used.

See also

terradish for fitting, conductance for the fitted surface as a raster, plot.terradish for the five diagnostic plot types, aic_table for ranking a model set, and mlpe_response_change for putting an MLPE covariate association on the response scale. See vignette("v01-getting-started", package = "terradish") for a walkthrough of reading these outputs and vignette("v04-model-comparison", package = "terradish") for anova() and AIC() in context.

Other model fitting: conductance(), terradish(), terradish_algorithm(), terradish_distance(), terradish_grid()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude), terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale.
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords[keep])

fit <- terradish(Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, data = surface,
                 conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
                 measurement_model = mlpe)

fit                    # coefficients, log-likelihood, and AIC
#> Conductance surface estimated by maximum likelihood
#> Call:   terradish(formula = Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, data = surface, 
#>     conductance_model = loglinear_conductance, measurement_model = mlpe)
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>    altitude  forestcover  
#>    -0.79207     -0.09613  
#> 
#> Loglikelihood: 1495.046 (6 degrees freedom)   AIC: -2978.092 
#> Convergence: converged | projected gradient: 1.93e-07 
summary(fit)           # adds standard errors, Wald tests, and the phi table
#> Conductance surface with 2531 vertices (31 focal) estimated by maximum likelihood
#> Call:   terradish(formula = Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, data = surface, 
#>     conductance_model = loglinear_conductance, measurement_model = mlpe)
#> 
#> Loglikelihood: 1495.046 (6 degrees freedom)
#> AIC: -2978.092 
#> 
#> Number of function calls: 19 
#> Number of optimization steps: 6 
#> Convergence: converged | projected gradient: 1.93e-07 
#> Norm of gradient at MLE: 2.57979e-07 
#> 
#> Nuisance parameters (conditional on fitted conductance surface; measurement-model scale):
#>        Estimate  Std. Error  Lower 95%  Upper 95%
#> alpha  -0.04900   0.01571    -0.07979   -0.01821 
#> beta    0.41808   0.01458     0.38951    0.44665 
#> tau     5.56654   0.23580     5.10439    6.02870 
#> rho     2.06189   0.27586     1.52121    2.60256 
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> altitude    -0.79207    0.15007  -5.278 1.31e-07 ***
#> forestcover -0.09613    0.19259  -0.499    0.618    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Correlation of Coefficients:
#>              altitude
#> forestcover 0.7879281

# Conductance coefficients are on the LOG scale, so exponentiate for a
# multiplicative reading: exp(theta) is the change in conductance per
# one-unit (one standard deviation, here) increase in the covariate.
coef(fit)
#>    altitude forestcover 
#> -0.79206795 -0.09612631 
exp(coef(fit))
#>    altitude forestcover 
#>   0.4529072   0.9083493 

logLik(fit)            # carries a df attribute, so AIC()/BIC() work
#> 'log Lik.' 1495.046 (df=6)
AIC(fit)               # compare only fits using the same response and likelihood family
#>       tau 
#> -2978.092 
head(fitted(fit)[, 1:4])     # fitted genetic distances
#>              [,1]         [,2]        [,3]         [,4]
#> [1,] -0.048999521 -0.005447103  0.14508089  0.040612727
#> [2,] -0.005447103 -0.048999521  0.15684956  0.052361591
#> [3,]  0.145080892  0.156849563 -0.04899952  0.091377571
#> [4,]  0.040612727  0.052361591  0.09137757 -0.048999521
#> [5,]  0.062776441  0.074524882  0.10982244  0.005662658
#> [6,] -0.008355229  0.007553196  0.13834571  0.033749003
head(residuals(fit)[, 1:4])  # observed minus fitted
#>              [,1]         [,2]        [,3]         [,4]
#> [1,]  0.048999521  0.014693842 -0.04113520  0.007279262
#> [2,]  0.014693842  0.048999521 -0.04828265 -0.003839283
#> [3,] -0.041135203 -0.048282645  0.04899952 -0.038938063
#> [4,]  0.007279262 -0.003839283 -0.03893806  0.048999521
#> [5,]  0.012324963  0.003186550 -0.04396978  0.032500892
#> [6,]  0.036041844  0.024135824 -0.01236317  0.031867978

# A nested comparison: is the interaction worth its parameter?
fit_int <- terradish(Fst ~ altitude * forestcover, data = surface,
                     conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
                     measurement_model = mlpe)
anova(fit, fit_int)
#> Likelihood ratio test: chi-square (1 df)
#> Null: ~ altitude + forestcover
#> Alt: ~ altitude + forestcover + altitude:forestcover
#>      logLik Df  ChiSq Df(ChiSq)  Pr(>Chi)    
#> Null 1495.0  6                               
#> Alt  1510.6  7 31.124         1 2.421e-08 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# }
